Meterpreter_2.0.259_mingw13_x64_metsrv.d.build_flags: cmake --build Release (-O3 -DNDEBUG) for i686-w64-mingw32 / x86_64-w64-mingw32 via upstream's toolsets/*.cmake; upstream USE_STATIC_MSVC_RUNTIMES=ON adds -static-libgcc -mwindows -fms-extensions -Wl,--enable-stdcall-fixup; BUILD_ALL=OFF with BUILD_METSRV=ON and BUILD_ARCH=Win32/x64
Meterpreter_2.0.259_mingw13_x64_metsrv.d.notes: Built through upstream's own MinGW cross-build (the CMake toolchain files in c/meterpreter/toolsets and the non-MSVC branch of workspace/CMakeLists.txt), which is the path Rapid7's own docker/Dockerfile provisions. It is not the toolchain Rapid7 distributes: their released binaries are MSVC v120_xp and make.bat pins v141_xp, neither of which exists on the windows-2022 runner, so no MSVC artefact is claimed here. metsrv statically contains an amalgamated zlib 1.0.4P (zlib.h:245 ZLIB_VERSION "1.0.4P", July 1996) with the PPP additions Z_PACKET_FLUSH, inflateIncomp and deflateOutputPending, so those functions are present under this family; it is a 1996 fork and does not duplicate the modern zlib in data/libzlib, which it shares two unnamed PicHashes with and no named one, and deflateOutputPending in the symbol table is the name that distinguishes the two. metsrv is C only: 61 functions are removed as compiler runtime on each architecture and all are plain MinGW glue. The two architectures share no PicHash of ten instructions or more with each other. One of the tree's 27 projects is built: ext_server_stdapi builds by this recipe but links as C++ and brings MinGW's C++ exception runtime in under this family's name, which needs a baseline round first and is recorded in the not-built table; the kiwi extension is not built at all, mimikatz being issue #60, though fetch.py still pins its submodule commit along with ReflectiveDLLInjection, COFFLoader and meterpreter-deps.
